task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-check of REQ-166's design after rework commit de27b0b addressing F1 (register/1 must ALSO attempt real instantiation, treating unresolved-import failure identically to a missing export, per req163 sec4's explicit assignment) and F2 (the false crash-propagation claim, now fixed with a Task.Supervisor-based monitored instantiation attempt, justified per req155's own one-supervisor-per-concern precedent). Verify independently -- re-run your own live wasmex experiments, do not trust the rework's self-report.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm register/1's redesigned two-stage flow (static check via compile/2+exports/1, THEN a real instantiation attempt via a Task.Supervisor-wrapped start_link/1) correctly treats an unresolved-import failure identically to a missing/malformed export -- rejected at registration with a structured error.

Independently reproduce the Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 + Task.yield/2 wrapping around start_link/1 on a module with an unresolved import yourself, and confirm the calling process survives (exit code 0) and receives the task outcome as an ordinary value, not a crash -- this is the load-bearing fix for F2.

Confirm the design states, and justifies, that the instantiation instance is started then immediately stopped (never kept alive) before register/1 returns, reconciled with decision 0014(e)'s per-invocation isolation principle.

Confirm the new dedicated Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor (or whatever the rework named it) is justified per an existing precedent (req155 sec4.4's one-supervisor-per-concern pattern is cited -- verify that citation is accurate by reading req155's actual sec4.4).
Confirm the re-derived 'never invocable' proof is sound: a registered_module() value is only constructed after BOTH stages pass.
Confirm req163-wasm-abi-choice.md section 4 is now cited and applied accurately -- no remaining contradiction.
All 6 real REQ-166 acceptance criteria still correctly mapped; zero literal Elixir code in the design doc.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: Independently re-verified rework commit de27b0b's fixes for both F1 and F2 from the original FAIL (commit 605bc5c). Both defects are genuinely resolved; the redesigned two-stage register/1 is sound, correctly cited, and implementable without ambiguity. No new blocking defects found.
verified_true: AC1: register/1's two-stage flow (stage 1: Wasmex.Module.compile/2 + exports/1 static check, unchanged and previously verified; stage 2: a real Wasmex.start_link/1 instantiation attempt, gated strictly on stage 1 passing) treats an unresolved-import instantiation failure identically to a missing/malformed export in the sense that matters: both are registration_error() variants ({:invalid_abi, _} vs {:instantiation_failed, _}), both returned from register/1's {:error, _} branch, and both block construction of a registered_module() value -- neither path reaches {:ok, registered_module()}. Rejected at registration in both cases, with a structured error naming the specific defect.

AC2 (load-bearing F2 fix): independently reproduced in a fresh MIX_ENV=test mix run script (not trusting the rework's self-report) against the real installed wasmex 0.15.1: calling Wasmex.start_link(%{bytes: bytes}) on a WAT module with an unresolved wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open import, wrapped in Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 + Task.yield/2 (a fresh :VerifySup Task.Supervisor started for this check), the calling process survived to the end of the script (exit code 0) and Task.yield/2 returned {:exit, {{:badmatch, {:error, "unknown import: `wasi_snapshot_preview1::path_open` has not been defined"}}, stacktrace}} as an ordinary task outcome -- exact match to the design's own §1.5/§5.1-step-7 claimed reproduction, including the precise error message wording the design's regex-style parse in §5.1 step 7 depends on. A control run against a conforming module returned {:ok, {:ok, pid}} with no crash, confirming the harness does not misclassify success.

AC3: design §3.1 explicitly states and justifies the start-then-stop decision (the stage-2 instance is started purely to observe start_link/1's outcome, then GenServer.stop/1'd inside the same task before register/1 returns; a later real invocation starts its own separate fresh instance). The three-part justification (breaking the uniform fresh-instance guarantee; holding a live Wasmtime instance for an unbounded unsupervised span; RegisteredModule carrying a pid that could die independently of the struct) is coherent and correctly reconciled with REQ-165's PluginHandler.run_guest/2 per-call fresh-instance pattern (verified directly in plugin_handler.ex lines 95-108: 'a fresh Wasmtime instance for this call only' / GenServer.stop on every path) and with decision 0014(e)'s discussion of WASM-08/WASM-13 per-invocation isolation (verified by reading 0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md lines 319-334 directly) -- 0014(e) discusses per-invocation isolation as the property to preserve for WASM guests under multi-tenancy, which the design's citation supports without contradiction.

AC4: verified req155-lua-wallclock-kill.md §4.4 (lines 137-213, read in full) verbatim: it justifies Letflow.Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor as a new dedicated Task.Supervisor precisely because this repo's own convention (Letflow.SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor and Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor already coexisting as separate supervisors for separate concerns) rejects sharing one supervisor across independently-reasoned-about subsystems 'for no offsetting benefit.' REQ-166's design §2.2 applies this same reasoning accurately (registration is a fourth, independent concern from dispatch/Lua-execution/sandbox-pool) to justify Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor. Citation is accurate, no drift.

AC5: the re-derived 'never invocable' proof (§4) is sound. It no longer rests on the false premise that register/1 never calls start_link/1; it correctly rests on (1) register/1 being the only function constructing a registered_module() value, only after BOTH stages pass, (2) RegisteredModule's @opaque annotation foreclosing external construction, and (3) the only two wasmex functions that can start a runnable instance (start_link/1, Instance.new/3) being reachable in register/1's own scope only inside stage 2, strictly after stage 1 already passed, and only via a Task.Supervisor-owned task whose instance is torn down before register/1 returns. No gap found: a rejected module's bytes reaching start_link/1 during register/1's own stage-2 attempt is exactly what produces the rejection, and structurally cannot leave behind a registered_module() or a live, caller-reachable instance.

AC6: independently re-read req163-wasm-abi-choice.md §4 in full (lines 226-252). It states verbatim that 'REQ-166's registration-time validation (§3.1) must attempt instantiation as part of registration and treat that failure identically to a missing required export: rejected at registration ... not merely at first invocation' -- explicitly assigning this duty to REQ-166's own register/1, naming the wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open surface only as the concrete fixture REQ-167's later test should target. The design's §4/§0/§1.1/§1.4 citations of this section are now accurate; no remaining contradiction with rework-1's prior misreading.

AC7: all 6 real REQ-166 acceptance criteria remain mapped in §6's traceability table, updated for the two-stage register/1 shape (AC3's row now explicitly covers the new instantiation-failure rejection case; AC4's row reflects register/1 succeeding only after both stages). Grepped the full design doc for def/defp/case-do/cond-do/with-do function-body patterns: zero matches. All 14 code fences contain only @spec/@type/@moduledoc/return-value-literal content -- no implementation bodies.
AC8: mix letflow.lint_handoffs run below; status field set to PASS/COMPLETED per the CRITICAL instruction.
